counterfactuals.2026-08-23T15:19:09: qwen lane declares 18432 (registry), each judge 4608 (>=1800s band). Avail before the qwen loaded reconstructs to ~24193 MB (observed 5761 + ~18 GB). Applying the admission test with RESERVE_MB=4608: qwen ADMITTED (24193-0-18432 = 5761 >= 4608); judge 1 REFUSED (24193-18432-4608 = 1153 < 4608), judges 2 and 3 likewise. One lane admitted, three left dispatchable, ZERO kills. All four 88-second deaths — the three at 251/133/129 MB and T783's unlabeled cull — do not happen. The 18 GB consumer is not invisible: it is CHARGED to the task that asked for it and is precisely why the batch did not fit.
counterfactuals.2026-07-29T02:37: L0 acts alone: -O ReleaseFast is the root-cause fix, and --rss-cap-mb bounds THAT process (the record's own arithmetic: caught 5 s before the cliff at a 4 GB cap). L2 refuses further lanes alongside a heavy build. L3 reads pressure_level=4 and compressor at 100% of segments — the panic's actual signature — closes admission and names zig pid 92604 at 12.5 GB. The FLOOR, at 6144 MB free, would have fired somewhere in the descent from 48 GB to 46 MB and killed the largest member of some runner's process group — on the corpus's evidence a 40-389 MB agent lane, not the 12.5 GB compiler. Futile, and the panic happens anyway.
